I received a call back at 9-9:30am letting me know the earliest I could come in and see the doctor was at 3:45pm. I sent photos to the office where they then showed the doctor and I was prescribed 2 medicines. They told me they wanted me to pick them up at the pharmacy and take them immediately. I didnt give them a pharmacy to call anything into, so I then had to tell them what the information WOULD be if they had called them in, along with asking what it was I would be taking as no one has told me anything about what type of medicine or why I was prescribed this. I was then told I could come in at 2:45, and then finally at 12:30. After rearranging my day, picking my child up from day care an hour early, and driving another 30 minutes to Plano I received reversal (dissolver) of the filler injection to relieve the pressure / blockage of hitting an artery. I received an apology and “call us tomorrow to let us know how it is.” I asked for a refund for the filler purchased, and was told that only 1/4 of the area filled was disolved and I would not receive a refund. The syringe was $680 - even 1/4 of that would be $170. I now also have to pay for the prescribed medications to take after the filler was injected in error. I have never written a review (good or bad) of any services / experiences I have had - but I felt like this was necessary to share with readers. I hope that other patients are able to seek guidance with this, or if they’ve experienced the same issues know that they are not alone. I don’t think any “rating on google”  can express my disappointment, frustration, and lack of professionalism I felt I received.

My first surgery with Dr. Jeff Angobaldo was back in July of 2020. I had a procedure that included TT, MR, liposuction to abdomen/flanks and breast lift with augmentation. I had a wound on one of my breast, tummy tuck, and BB which I understand PS has no control over. He stated that it could be fixed with a separate procedure! (Sigh). I was very hesitant but I decided to go ahead and get a second procedure for breast reduction. I went to a consultation which I asked about changing my implants (310 cc to a 200 or 250 cc) to bring me down to a full C. I showed him inspiration pics which he explained that changing the size wouldn’t make a difference since I had a lot of breast tissue so he would just remove breast tissue. I didn’t understand this much but I agreed since I was influenced by his surgeon recommendation. During preop I shared this information with his nurses and they advised me to be persistent on what I wanted because he tends to do what he believes would look good instead of listening to his patients desires. With this I made sure to repeat myself when stating I wanted to be a full C after the procedure. I had my second procedure with him on May 2023. During my follow up appointments I expressed that I felt my right breast was larger than my left . His MA kept insisting that it was swelling and to give it time. For the first 2-3 follow up appointment I didn’t see Dr Angobaldo only his MAs. During one of these appointments I let them know that I was having a fluid leak from one of my breast and they applied Manuka honey and gauze on it. At a later appointment I finally saw Dr A and he prescribed me antibiotics for this reason, this is when I finally got to express my concern over my breast size. (At this time I was 3 months PO). He suggested that he could perform a revision on both breast and offered to remove both implants. At this point I was very irritated and annoyed since I got this second procedure to fix the first one. In total the first procedure was $18,500 the, awake revision was $250 and this last procedure was a total of about $5,000 (breast reduction and lipo to axillary area and abdomen). These costs don’t include medications and aftercare needs! In my mind that was what I was thinking, I’ve already spent all this money and now he wants to put me through a third procedure with him. He was able to tell that I was upset and recommended that I think about it and bring it back up at my 6 month follow up. After this follow up, front office scheduled me for a 6 month follow up. At this point I just took a loss and am not making any attempts to see him again.

service_quality_in_session.snippet:
***Update***

I’m updating this review after reading Dr. Toledo’s reply, which is completely inaccurate and misleading. To set the record straight: not once did he ask any mental health questions, perform any kind of evaluation, or have the right to make such a reckless claim about me.

My appointment lasted less than 10 minutes total - not “almost an hour” as he claims. The imaging portion took under a minute, and the moment I asked to see a few small adjustments, he became visibly impatient and dismissive. He walked out and returned saying he “can’t fix my brain” and that I’d be “nitpicking every angle.” That comment was degrading, completely uncalled for, and crossed every line of professionalism.

Declining a surgery is one thing. Lying publicly about a patient’s mental health to justify disrespectful behavior is another. His response is not only dishonest but manipulative, and it shows exactly the type of arrogance I experienced in that room. I stand by every single word of my review..no patient deserves to be spoken to or treated this way.

------------------------------------

I am deeply hurt and disappointed by my recent consultation with Dr. Toledo. I previously had a minor surgery with him back in June that went very well, so I was excited to come back for a rhinoplasty consultation. Sadly, this experience left me in tears and I’ve never looked at myself this way the way I’ve been insulted by someone I trusted so much.

At first, he was direct, which I appreciated because not a lot of doctors are..I’ll give him that. But once we got to the imaging, things went downhill. He spent about 10 secs creating one potential outcome on the computer and expected me to accept it without further discussion. When I asked questions and requested a few tweaks so I could see every angle, he became dismissive. The entire “consult” was 5 mins including the time I walked in the door and he came in the room, to me sitting down for imaging.

Dr. Toledo left the room, then came back sighing and told his nurse he “can’t perform on me” because I “have body dysmorphia.” He then said he “can’t fix my brain” and grabbed a mirror saying I’d be “nitpicking every angle of my nose”. This was all because I wanted a consultation longer than a few mins to make sure I understood the results before investing my hard-earned money for something I’ve wanted for my birthday/grad/Christmas gift to myself. He said “he doesn’t perform on people like that” implying there’s something wrong with me. I was so shocked and hurt.

I took off work early for this appointment and was genuinely excited, but instead I was insulted and left in tears. I never expected this from anyone especially a doctor I trusted. No patient deserves to be treated this way. I will also be reporting this experience to the medical board.

I complained a week later to staff during my follow-up visit, telling them about how bad that experience was.  I never returned for my post op photos. The treatment I received after waking still haunts me today. We all don’t have the same pain tolerances. His comment was insensitive and off putting. He speaks to you as though you’re LUCKY to even speak with him at all. Don’t ask a question, unless you want him to shut it down as though you are a child asking for dessert before dinner. His staff seems to try to overcompensate  for his lack of empathy, but it  wasn’t enough. I hope he can gain better perspective of how to return to treating patients with compassion and exemplify ethical behavior to clients that are arriving already feeling eager for support.

I’m writing this on behalf of my friend because I’ve been with her through her rhinoplasty journey with Dr. Mani and have seen her experience firsthand.

Before surgery, she had a consultation where she clearly communicated wanting a narrower nose, smaller tip, reduced dorsal hump, and most importantly narrower nostrils.

She is now about 10.5 weeks post-op and, from what I’ve seen, the changes are very minimal. The main visible difference is that her dorsal hump is gone, but overall her nose still looks very similar in width, especially around the bridge and nostrils. Even when comparing before and after photos, the nostril width looks essentially unchanged.

I’ve also noticed that she has been really unhappy with her results since the cast came off. At first it seemed okay due to swelling, but as time passed she felt like her nose didn’t reflect what she expected or what was discussed. The tip also looks more pointed than before, which she doesn’t like.

She also mentioned concerns about follow-up care, including having to bring up taping herself despite having thicker skin, and feeling like guidance after cast removal wasn’t very proactive.

On top of that, there are visible signs of healing like scarring and discoloration that have added to her frustration.

She paid around $11K for the procedure and, from both her perspective and mine as someone close to her, she feels disappointed with the outcome and wishes she had had a different result or more alignment with what was originally discussed.

I’m sharing this because I think people should hear real experiences when considering something as big as a rhinoplasty with Dr. Mani.

I also had body contouring, and there was essentially no time spent discussing desired shape or problem areas. Dr Raphael was in and out. I’m thankful for the care I received and the professionalism of everyone, but I now have many revisions to my results that I will need, as well as outcomes that I unfortunately can’t change, but couldve been avoided with better communication. If you’re receiving care her and spending this kind of money, I’d recommend making sure that the details are mulled over, and you have a list of specifics, as well as questions or concerns. These surgery’s are a big deal.

frontline_communication.snippet:
I called this clinic to schedule a breast augmentation consultation with Dr. Dulin. When I mentioned I’m a transgender woman using BCBS insurance, the staff member told me they wouldn’t accept it — not because it wasn’t covered, but because they don’t want to “discriminate against cisgender patients.”

She said, verbatim: “They don’t cover it for cisgender people, so we don’t take it for transgender people, because that’s discrimination against our cisgender patients.” When I replied that it seemed odd, she snapped back, “No it’s not,” in a flat tone.

This clinic advertises gender-affirming care through the International Center for Transgender Care. But if this is how they treat transgender patients — rejecting valid insurance coverage and justifying it with a backwards idea of ‘equality’ — then it’s not affirming, it’s performative.

I’ve since reported the experience to my insurance company. I hope this helps other trans patients avoid the same hurt and disappointment. Respect matters.

The staff of the surgical clinic were very professional and made me as comfortable as possible before and after the surgery. It was after the surgeries that the behavior of the clinic changed. All of the post-operative appointments were incredibly brief. This was especially distressing during the first post-operative appointment when I was in a lot of pain. The physician examined me for five minutes before having me rushed out of the office. I was left with many concerns and questions that unnecessarily had to be addressed through e-mail. On two occasions I have had to send correspondence to get answers to concerns that could have easily been addressed had the physician given me the time. Every following pre-operative visit has been a similar five-minute visit that has been very disrespectful of the time it takes me to visit the clinic. I recommend having your primary care physician being aware of the procedures you will be getting. Especially if you suffer from any degree of respiratory illness as this plastic surgery clinic is not knowledgeable about how serious these complications can be. The combination of my procedures put me in a position where an aerosolized inhaler was very difficult to use as it was painful to inhale properly. This is information that should be included in the post-operative documentation as obtaining a nebulizer after the fact is not a feat that can be done quickly. Ultimately, I have my reservations about this plastic surgery clinic as their bedside manner went from top-notch in the surgery clinic to disappointingly unprofessional on the administrative side. While still experiencing respiratory distress from the results of the procedure I am left with a lot of doubt as to whether the clinic has the patient's best interest in mind. If you choose to use this clinic please make sure to be informed of the procedures you desire and your own medical history very well as they will proceed with what you pay for regardless of the contraindications.

I got a lower blepharoplasty done here in December, 2024. I was 31 and had very mild under eye bags and I thoroughly regret this procedure.
I naturally had a lot of volume under my eyes and upper cheek areas and it was a beautiful look. Naive to plastic surgery or methods, my hope and expectations were to remove the under eye bags while preserving my natural youthful look.

At my consultation Dr. Robert’s spent very little time in the room with me, he did not ask to see a photo before the natural aging process, and he asked me who I got the under eye bags from since I was kind of young for them. I felt very insecure in that room, but looking back I realize I did not need the surgery and there are far less invasive methods of targeting a little under eye sagging. Of course, this man is running a business and his job is to treat his patients, but my main concern here is that he employs antiquated methods for lower blepharoplasty.

Upon further research (sadly, after the fact) most surgeons reposition the fat, instead of removing it. This preserves the volume and natural contouring.
He just completely took mine and now my whole face looks different, especially my smile. I now hate taking pictures and worry how my face will age with the very generous volume loss that was stripped from the area.

My face isn’t botched by any means, but I wish he had spent more time with me asking me questions and getting to know what my expectations were. The only thing he had mentioned was “it’s not going to get rid of the lines.”
What he failed to mention was that it would greatly exaggerate the line that ARE there, and add NEW lines with the generous volume that was removed. My volume (some women spend tons of money to get) is gone, and I now look 5 years older than before the surgery and it’s devastating.

For reference, these pictures are taken exactly one year apart. 31->32 years old.

If you are considering lower blepharoplasty at this clinic, I would reconsider and choose a surgeon who truly cares.

In the beginning of this year, I underwent a BBL procedure. Shortly after, I was diagnosed with a PULMONARY EMBOLISM- a life threatening condition that required immediate medical intervention. My boyfriend previously shared a brief review of what followed after I noticed the symptoms began to surface, but now that I’ve completed all required testings and bloodwork, and have met with both my PCP and hematologist for answers, as Dr. Walker advised, I feel it’s important to finally speak for myself.

After my surgery, before my boyfriend wrote a review, I sometimes wasn’t getting responses to my emails and had to call quite a few times. I still have those unanswered emails in my mail. After the review was posted, I no longer had problems with getting my emails answered. At one point, I experienced an issue after hours and called the after hours line. I’m not sure whether the lady I spoke with called Dr. Walker, (I don’t know the exact process they use to get in touch with him), but she tried reaching out to him three times, and he did not respond. She followed up with me each attempt as she mentioned before ending the call that I should expect a call from him within approximately 20 minutes. I’m very understanding, so by the third attempt, I told her it was okay, that I understand he may have been occupied or addressing other urgent matters at that time and ended up handling it myself.

Prior to the pulmonary embolism, I developed swelling and mild bruising below my right knee. Nearly 6 months after surgery, the swelling persists, and, sometimes, only subsides with the use of compression socks. It becomes particularly evident when my leg is exposed, serving as a constant reminder of everything I went through. Notably, there was no prior history of swelling in this region, it was one of the earliest indicators of the pulmonary embolism that followed.

A moment that still stands out to me was when I consulted Dr. Walker about firm, painful bumps, forming under my skin by my abdomen. Despite my concern and specific questions about fibrosis, he assured me it wasn’t the case. That brought me a great sense of relief. However, upon bringing the issue to my PCP, since the affected area showed no signs of improvement, a later evaluation confirmed it was fibrosis. Something that made me question the accuracy of his assessment and overall care.

Beyond that, I was deeply disappointed with my surgical results.

I was genuinely excited to get this BBL, but unfortunately, what I experienced was FAR from what I hoped. I waited to write this review until I completed all necessary testing and blood-work because I wanted to share the honest truth. There is SO much more I could share, but it’s too much to put into words. Ultimately, everyone is human and errors are inevitable. I hope that anyone considering a procedure like this will not make the mistake I did. Make sure to ask thorough questions, not just surface level ones. Research your surgeon carefully, and make sure you choose someone who truly cares, not just someone who says they do.

frontline_communication.snippet:
My girlfriend recently had a BBL with Dr. Walker. We noticed some concerning symptoms, including, swelling in both feet, mild bruising with additional swelling on the lower right part of her leg, just below the knee, and shortness of breath/chest pain. Upon evaluation at the ER, she was diagnosed with a PULMONARY EMBOLISM—a LIFE-THREATENING CONDITION.

Before taking her to the ER, concerned, she immediately called the office after noticing her symptoms. She explained the swelling in her feet and the bruising with swelling below her knees to the woman she spoke with on the phone, I believe it was the receptionist. She was then placed on hold while the lady informed Dr. Walker about the situation. Afterward, my girlfriend was asked to send pictures, which she promptly did. The lady then said that Dr. Walker wanted her to elevate her feet and wear compression socks. If my girlfriend hadn’t spoken up about her chest pain and shortness of breath, I honestly don’t know if she would still be here with us today. It was only after she reported shortness of breath/chest pain that she was finally advised to go to the ER. Throughout the entire process, she constantly asked questions and sought clear instructions on how to proceed. Despite the seriousness of her symptoms, she was repeatedly placed on hold by the lady she was speaking with on the phone.

Upon receiving instructions to go to the ER, I immediately rushed her there. Blood work results indicated the PRESENCE OF BLOOD CLOTS, and a CT scan confirmed what we FEARED—she had a PULMONARY EMBOLISM a LIFE-THREATENING CONDITION , but by the grace of God, she is still here with us.

I sincerely urge you to do your research before selecting a surgeon. During your consultation, don’t hesitate to ask comprehensive questions to ensure you fully understand your options and the care being provided.

I had a wound on one of my breast, tummy tuck, and BB which I understand PS has no control over. I went back a couple weeks after for a awake revision of my wound scars on my breast and BB which he explained he could fix, during this follow up I expressed that I was unhappy with the size of implants. I had requested to stay at a size D or DD with cleavage during my consultation and preop appointment although I ended up with a size DDD which was very noticeable since I am a tiny girl 4 feet 9 in. He stated that it could be fixed with a separate procedure! (Sigh). I was very hesitant but I decided to go ahead and get a second procedure for breast reduction. I went to a consultation which I asked about changing my implants (310 cc to a 200 or 250 cc) to bring me down to a full C. I showed him inspiration pics which he explained that changing the size wouldn’t make a difference since I had a lot of breast tissue so he would just remove breast tissue. I didn’t understand this much but I agreed since I was influenced by his surgeon recommendation. During preop I shared this information with his nurses and they advised me to be persistent on what I wanted because he tends to do what he believes would look good instead of listening to his patients desires. With this I made sure to repeat myself when stating I wanted to be a full C after the procedure. I had my second procedure with him on May 2023. During my follow up appointments I expressed that I felt my right breast was larger than my left . His MA kept insisting that it was swelling and to give it time. For the first 2-3 follow up appointment I didn’t see Dr Angobaldo only his MAs. During one of these appointments I let them know that I was having a fluid leak from one of my breast and they applied Manuka honey and gauze on it. At a later appointment I finally saw Dr A and he prescribed me antibiotics for this reason, this is when I finally got to express my concern over my breast size. (At this time I was 3 months PO). He suggested that he could perform a revision on both breast and offered to remove both implants. At this point I was very irritated and annoyed since I got this second procedure to fix the first one. In total the first procedure was $18,500 the, awake revision was $250 and this last procedure was a total of about $5,000 (breast reduction and lipo to axillary area and abdomen). These costs don’t include medications and aftercare needs! In my mind that was what I was thinking, I’ve already spent all this money and now he wants to put me through a third procedure with him. He was able to tell that I was upset and recommended that I think about it and bring it back up at my 6 month follow up. After this follow up, front office scheduled me for a 6 month follow up. Once it got closer to that date they have changed my appointment last minute twice. And they told me that a 3rd revision would be about $1,200. At this point I just took a loss and am not making any attempts to see him again.

P.S. my BB scar was never fixed I had to cover it up with a tattoo.
